themes.description: Total dedication to God and following Christ
Devotion to the Blessed Virgin Mary
Role and responsibilities of Superior General
Service to the poor and marginalized

sections.title: Our Consecration
sections.text: Co 2:1-2 "It is not ourselves that we are preaching, but Christ Jesus as the Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus' sake."

sections.title: Our Vocation
sections.text: Tm 4:2-5 "I am the good shepherd; the good shepherd is one who lays down his life for his sheep." Jn 10:11

sections.title: Our Response
sections.text: The sisters, true to their humble origins, want to live the poverty and the simplicity of the Gospel; genuine charity is rooted in humility. But self-effacement does not rule out the tranquil daring of those who trust in God alone.

sections.title: Consecration to God
sections.text: St. Paul is the patron of the Congregation. The spirituality of the Sisters of St. Paul is based on his epistles: Christocentric spirituality expressed by a deep love for Christ and an ardent zeal for his Gospel; Paschal spirituality which discovers in mortification and death the seed of new life and unending joy. The sisters recognize the action of God in their origins and their history. They find there an incentive to spend themselves with greater apostolic zeal and to open themselves to the paschal mystery in their lives.

sections.title: Perseverance
sections.text: From the beginning, the Congregation has been placed under the protection of the Virgin Mary. The sisters seek to know her better through Holy Scripture and the teaching of the Church; they find in Mary the model of: deep faith and complete trust, absolute conformity to the plan of God, perfect participation in the mystery of salvation, thoughtful, warmhearted service of others.

sections.title: Following Christ
sections.text: The Sisters of St. Paul were founded to meet the needs of their fellowmen and, from the start, have recognized in each one of them, the person of Our Lord Jesus Christ. "In so far as you did this to one of the least of these brothers of mine, you did it to me". Dedicated by foundation to education, the care of the sick and the underprivileged, they are available for all forms of activity within these fields. Whatever kind of work they may be engaged in, the sisters keep in mind that their first aim in life is to further the growth of the kingdom of God.

sections.title: Apostolic Love
sections.text: As servant of the poor throughout the world, the Congregation has no territorial preference, and the far-off missions reap the benefit of its zeal. It responds with fidelity to the call of the Church, serving the needs of mankind with a special love for the most neglected. The sending to the far-off missions depends on a personal option clearly expressed by the sister. Commitment

sections.title: Call to Holiness
sections.text: The Sisters of St. Paul bind themselves by public vows of chastity, poverty, and obedience to live a life consecrated to Christ in the Church. These vows are at first temporary, then perpetual. In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, Lord Jesus, in the power of your Spirit I desire to consecrate myself to the kingdom of the Father in the service of mankind. United in your sacrifice of praise I vow chastity, poverty, and obedience (for one year, forever) in the Congregation of the Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres into the hands of Reverend Mother General (1) and I bind myself to live according to the rule of life of this Congregation. Grant me, Lord, the grace to fulfill this offering which I now make Enable me to remain faithful until your return. Amen. "You have seduced me, Yahweh, and I have let myself be seduced; You have overpowered me: you were the stronger." Jr 20:7 "I was sitting at home and the elders of Judah Were sitting with me, when the hand of the Lord Yahweh fell on me." Ez 8:1 "See, I have branded you on the palms of my hands." Is 49:16 "All that exists comes from him; all is by him and for him. To him be glory for ever!" Rm 11:36 "Think of God's mercy, my brothers and worship him, I beg you, in a way that is worthy of thinking beings, by offering your bodies as a holy sacrifice, truly pleasing to God." Rm 12:1 "And for their sake I consecrate myself so that they may be consecrated in truth." Jn 17:19 Consecration

sections.title: Baptismal Consecration
sections.text: Consecration is inspired by the charity that God pours into our hearts. This consecration pledges us to love God and all men as perfectly as possible; it is expressed by the profession of chastity, poverty and obedience. Consecration and Baptism

sections.title: Religious Profession
sections.text: Consecration by the vows of religion manifests baptismal consecration in a special manner and more fully by the free, public, and definitive commitment to belong to God and to live for God.

sections.title: Perpetual Vows
sections.text: This consecration, like baptismal consecration, is stamped with the paschal seal. It impels us to lose our life that we may find it. With Christ, through the Spirit, the person who is consecrated surrenders herself to the Father in an act of pure love. The profession of evangelical counsels is an act of adoration and a sacrifice which draws its strength from the sacrifice of Christ. Consecration and Apostolate

sections.title: Temporary Vows
sections.text: The Sisters of St. Paul show that they belong to the Lord by the gift of themselves to others. Their apostolic witness flows from their consecration and bears its imprint. Following in the footsteps of Christ Jesus, of the first Apostles and of St. Paul, the sisters live in the world, their hearts burning with love. The sisters, by their consecration, bear witness to the new and everlasting life to which all men are called; their presence is a reminder of the universal call to holiness. The sisters belong to the Lord. This is evident in their whole life by their manner of being and acting. The Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres wear the habit of their Institute as sign of their consecration and as witness to poverty. Profession

sections.title: Marian Consecration
sections.text: At the moment of profession, the self-oblation which the religious makes in response to God's call, authenticated in the Church by the competent Superiors, takes on the nature of a consecration. Profession involves a contract: the sister undertakes to participate actively in the life of the Congregation of which she is now a member with rights and duties defined by law (C 654); and the Congregation undertakes to provide the professed sister with the conditions required for the living of her life as a consecrated person. The profession of evangelical counsels is an act of worship, an ecclesial act. As such, it gives praise to the Father, through the Son, in the Spirit, and benefits the whole Mystical Body. The sisters give a warm welcome to the newly professed members and undertake to live with them an authentic consecrated life; they help one another to remain faithful to their commitment. Conscious that their consecration is lived in the Congregation which has accepted them, they are loyal to one another, and faithful to the aim and spirit of the Sisters of St. Paul in all places and circumstances. The sisters renew their vows together on the Feast of the Oblation of Our Lord in the temple (Feb 2). In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, Lord Jesus, in your presence, I renew the vows of chastity, poverty and obedience, which I have made in the Congregation of the Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres. Make me grow in your love and help me to remain faithful until your return. Amen. Firmly resolved to be true to her word given to God and to her Congregation, the sister frequently renews her commitment. "Take care therefore not to forget the convenant which Yahweh your God has made with you... for Yahweh your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God." Dt 4:23-24 "I will betroth you to myself forever, betroth you with integrity and justice, with tenderness and love; I will betroth you to myself with faithfulness, and you will come to know Yahweh." Ho 2:21-22 "My Beloved is mine and I am his." Sg 2:16 "You see, the jealousy that I feel for you is God's own jealousy: I arranged for you to marry Christ so that I might give you away as a chaste virgin to this one husband."

sections.title: Gift of Chastity
sections.text: The vow of chastity comprises a free and voluntary choice of celibacy and of perfect continence in view of the kingdom of heaven (C 599). Marriage is the sign of the union of Christ and the Church but consecrated chastity is the manifestation of the reality of the New Covenant in a clearer and fuller way. Motivation and Requirements

sections.title: Undivided Heart
sections.text: It is the love for Christ above all else which motivates our choice of consecrated virginity as a state of life; this love for Christ is strong, total, undivided, and enables us to persevere in the chosen path. Our belonging to Christ, now sealed by the vow of chastity, adds a new dimension to the obligation to be chaste. Love is purified and strengthened through our faithful correspondence to the graces of each day and progressively God takes possession of our heart. The demands of God's love are limitless and she who loves can never do enough. Community of Consecrated Persons

sections.title: Witness of Chastity
sections.text: A heart surrendered to God becomes free to love all men as God loves them. It is in the climate of their consecration that the community life of the Sisters of St. Paul unfolds. Considerate, fraternal affection unites all the Sisters and brings them mutual support and the incentive necessary to their life of charity. Coming from God, true friendship leads back to him and goes out to others. Respect for each person contributes to more genuine relationships within the community. Consecrated Chastity and Apostolate

sections.title: Living Chastity
sections.text: Correspondence with God's love fulfills the longings of the human heart created for love. It keeps the faculties in balance and brings peace and joy. Consecrated chastity is a source of spiritual fruitfulness, no matter how hidden one's task may be. Marriage and religious life are two states of the Christian life which are enriched by the reciprocity of support and example in the daily struggle for fidelity. The sisters are cordial and approachable, and with kindness and simplicity, they draw from the inexhaustible resources of charity so as to effectively serve their fellowmen, especially the most needy. With a fully detached and humble heart, abounding in patience and love, the Sisters of St. Paul reveres in the most neglected, the suffering members of Jesus Christ. Solitude and Silence

sections.title: Means of Fidelity
sections.text: A courageously embraced solitude must go hand in hand with a life of consecrated chastity. This requires maturity and equilibrium. Those who abandon themselves totally to God in prayer and interior silence are more receptive to his grace so as to lead a life of fidelity. Destined by their apostolic vocation to live in the world, the sisters set aside time devoted to prayer and silence in order to renew their intimacy with the Lord. By progressive control of the imagination and the memory, they grow in ever greater openness to God's love. Consecrated Chastity lived in faith

sections.title: Formation in Chastity
sections.text: Perfect chastity is a gift of God. Only in humility and poverty, after the example of the Virgin Mary, can this gift be kept. The eye of faith sees the presence of God in all events and recognizes the image of God in every man, a brother redeemed by Christ. Voluntary asceticism, motivated by love, leads to the gift of oneself. Apostolic life keeps the fire of charity burning and rekindles it. Sacramental life is the unfailing source of grace and to partake of the Body and Blood of the Lord is to eat the food of eternal life. The sisters are able to discern in their life any tendencies to escapism, selfishness or seeking for compensation; they judiciously select their relaxations and are prudent and reserved in their contacts outside the community. "His state was divine, yet he did not cling to his equality with God but emptied himself to assume the condition of a slave, and became as men are..." Ph 2:6-7 "Remember how generous the Lord Jesus was: he was rich, but he became poor for your sake, to make you rich out of his poverty."

sections.title: Gospel Poverty
sections.text: By the profession of the poverty the sisters manifest that they acknowledge God as their sovereign and only good. In him they place their hope and expect from his goodness the true riches of the kingdom of heaven. The experience of God's love is a prerequisite for detachment from earthly goods. The person who is voluntarily poor conforms her life to Jesus Christ, poor from the crib to the cross. Jesus teaches us dependence on the Father in abandonment and trust. He proclaims the blessedness of the poor and invites us to sell all so as to possess the priceless treasure of the kingdom of heaven. Above all, Christ proposes himself as our model when he teaches us that genuine poverty comes from the heart: "....learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for you souls". Matter of the Vow

sections.title: Spirit of Poverty
sections.text: The Sisters of St. Paul, by their vow of poverty, renounce the right to use and dispose of temporal goods licitly without the permission of the lawful Superiors. They may not contract debts or obligations without permission of the same Superiors. Nevertheless, each sister retains the ownership of her property and the possibility of acquiring more. However, before her temporary profession she cedes the administration of these goods to whomsoever she wishes and freely disposes of their use and revenues. Before her perpetual profession each sister makes a will that is also valid in civil law. The modification of these dispositions and any act concerning her temporal goods require the authorization of the Superior General (C 668). The sisters who wish to do so, may renounce their property after their perpetual profession with the authorization of the Superior General. The salary which the sisters receive, all income from their own work, pensions and retirement benefits, as well as any gifts offered them belong by right to the community. The dowry is optional; it is inalienable. The giving up of material goods would be meaningless without the continual gift of self to God and to others. Renunciation of material goods both signifies and stimulates the gift of self. Collective Poverty

sections.title: Common Life
sections.text: For the Congregation of the Sisters of St. Paul the holding of goods in common is the expression of the charity of its members as it was for the early Christian community. The sharing of material goods is one of the visible aspects of evangelical fraternity. The life-style of the communities is simple, sober and poor, befitting the condition of persons consecrated to God. The sisters willingly adapt themselves to all circumstances of life. This is one form of their poverty. All the sisters are answerable for the poverty of the community and, from time to time, they question themselves regarding their life of poverty. Each sister is aware of the value of things and has respect for what belongs to the community. Together the sisters determine what they can do without so as to help those who are in need. The things that belong to the community are for the use of all, but no individual is their owner. Those required for work or apostolate are not personal belongings. The living quarters of the community are modest and soberly furnished. The houses are hospitable and open to the needs of the apostolate with due regard for what is essential to the living of community life.

sections.title: Use of Goods
sections.text: Justice and charity regulate the use of material goods in the community. Confidence in God dispels all excessive anxiety in the administration of the community property, but does not dispense with the prudence which the management of the goods of the poor requires. A spirit of mutual assistance flows from the houses to the Province, from the Province to the Generalate, so that those who have more share with those who have less. The community provides for the needs of each sister. A genuine spirit of charity and equity motivates the sisters and those in charge. Personal Poverty

sections.title: Permission for Use
sections.text: The sisters aspire to true poverty of heart, of which joy is the sign. The person who is voluntarily poor is always content with what she receives, and shares what she has. In all events, the hope that fills her makes her rise above the changing circumstances of this life. Over and above the renunciation of her property, the abnegation of common life, and dependence on Superiors, each sister responds to the promptings of grace by a more personal detachment. The person who is poor in heart, relying on God, always finds opportunity to take the lowest place. Full of peace and joy she accepts her personal limitations as well as the cares of the apostolate. She gladly shares her knowledge, gives of her time and spends herself, willingly losing all in order to find Jesus Christ. Each sister tries sincerely to make her poverty real; she makes known her needs and accepts what she is given. A permission obtained does not dispense from the demands of personal poverty which grace inspires her to practice. The sisters may dispose of a sum of money for their work and their traveling expenses but they submit a statement of money spent. Those in charge of funds account for them to the authority concerned. In the interest of justice, the sisters do not claim any privilege. They respect all those who work, pay just wages and observe the social laws. Work

sections.title: Personal Property
sections.text: Since the Congregation was founded, the sisters, following the example of St. Paul, have worked for a living. Thus, they participate with their fellowmen in the work of creation and in the redemption of the world. Respect for others, a sense of cooperation, discipline and solidarity, as well as sufficient knowledge in matters of social justice, are indispensable for teamwork. Wherever they work, the sisters wish to make the love of Christ present. The sisters contribute to the support of the community which includes young sisters in formation, aged members.... In their daily work, they are careful to avoid waste of time and things. Each sister is willing to accept the lowliest tasks and she does her share of the household work. No one allows work to prevail over her interior liberty.

sections.title: Witness of Poverty
sections.text: After her work, the sister needs to relax. Judicious planning should make it possible for all the sisters to have sufficient time for rest, spiritual renewal, intellectual and artistic pursuits, and other personal interests. The sisters use their time of relaxation in such a way as to give better service. This relaxation is in keeping with their condition as poor people. "Being as all men are, he was humbler yet, even to accepting death, death on a cross. But God raised him high and gave him the name which is above all other names." Ph 2:8-9 "As by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by one man's obedience many will be made righteous." Rm 5:19 "But Jesus said: 'My food is to do the will of the one who sent me, and to complete his work.' " Jn 4:34 "But the world must be brought to know that I love the Father and that I am doing exactly what the Father told me." Jn 14:31 "If you keep my commandments you will remain in my love, just as I have kept my Father's commandments and remain in his love." Jn 15:10 "I am the handmaid of the Lord,' said Mary 'let what you have said be done to me.' " Lk 1:38 Theologal Obedience

sections.title: Call to Obedience
sections.text: The Son united to the Father in the Spirit of love redeemed the world by obeying even to the death on the cross. The Sisters of St. Paul, under the impulse of the Holy Spirit, conform their lives to the filial obedience of Christ and continue it in the Mystical Body. By the profession of obedience, they irrevocably abandon their will to God and adhere to his salvific will. Initiated at their baptism into the mystery of filial obedience they now, in a voluntary and definitive manner, bind themselves to it by vow.

sections.title: Spirit of Obedience
sections.text: Obedience has its roots in faith. She who has faith is enlightened interiorly by the Spirit and discerns God's will in events and people. Free and voluntary obedience, animated by hope and motivated by love, configures her to Christ the Servant. Christ's whole life is a living out of the Father's plan, in the Spirit, for the salvation of the world.

sections.title: Obedience to Superiors
sections.text: The profession of obedience strengthens the personal alliance established between God and the baptized. If Christ invites us by his grace to conform our will of the Father throughout our whole life and follow him to the cross, he also promises to lead us by his Spirit to greater union with him. Obligation of the Vow

sections.title: Dialogue in Obedience
sections.text: By their vow of obedience, the Sisters of St. Paul promise to obey the Church in the person of the Sovereign Pontiff and their Lawful Superiors when they command in accordance with the Constitutions of the Congregation (C 601). Changes of assignment are outstanding moments in a life of obedience and are lived in faith. At such times, Superior and sister are united in seeking the will of God. In a serious case and prudently, the Major Superior may require obedience in the name of the Lord, which would then be binding in virtue of the vow. Obedience and Community Life

sections.title: Responsible Obedience
sections.text: The sisters seek the will of God in community with clearsightedness and perseverance. To this end, Superiors and sisters, united in charity, help one another in an atmosphere of mutual trust. The Superior's final decision calls for a courageous response and unites all the members of the community in obedience. In the awareness that she has surrendered to God her right to lead an independent life, the sister seeks in encounters with her local Superior the means to live in union with the will of God. She regularly submits her schedule, her practice of poverty, her participation in common life, her health problems. She gives an account of her work and apostolate. Spiritual matters may be discussed if the sister so desires. Within the context of obedience, each sister assumes responsibility for all her acts. Superior and sisters have a keen sense of co-responsibility in the act of obedience.

sections.title: Obedience to Church
sections.text: The interior attitude of the Superior is that of Christ Jesus who came to serve. She is alert to detect the workings of the Spirit in each one of her sisters. She knows how to listen, and when need be, she also knows how to make decisions. In all humility, she herself accepts the advice of her Superiors and follows the indications of Providence. Prayer and the fraternal support of her community give her and all her sisters the strength to correspond with God's will. The Superior encourages initiative, fosters a spirit of mutual respect and trust, and takes into consideration the suggestions of the sisters regarding the life of the community. On the other hand, the sisters cooperate with the Superior while acknowledging her authority; nevertheless, in case of serious difficulty, they may always have recourse to the Major Superiors. Obedience and Apostolate

sections.title: Obedience to Constitutions
sections.text: In their apostolic work, the Sisters of St. Paul through their free and voluntary consecrated obedience assume the limitations and sufferings inherent in the human condition thus uniting them to the redemptive mystery of Christ who for us became obedient even unto death. They welcome the different events of their life as encounters with the living God. "I give you a new commandment: love one another; just as I have loved you, you also must love one another. By this love you have for one another, everyone will know that you are my disciples." Jn 13:34-35 "So this is commandment that he has given us, that anyone who loves God must also love his brother."

sections.title: Community Life
sections.text: God is love. He created man in his image to enable him to participate in his life of love. The revelation of the mystery of the Trinity unveils to us the perfect relationship of love which unites the three divine Persons while maintaining their distinction. The Father communicates his love to us through the Holy Spirit that we may love him and love one another as Jesus Christ has loved us. In this way, we tend toward the end for which we were created.

sections.title: Love and Unity
sections.text: The love of God was manifested in Jesus Christ who became incarnate for our redemption. By his death and resurrection Jesus became the eldest of many brothers. The law of love is, therefore, the charter of the fraternal community founded on Christ. We have been redeemed and gathered together in Jesus Christ. Already on this earth we live in charity and aspire to the kingdom of eternal communion in the love that will never pass away. Community Life

sections.title: Sharing Life
sections.text: The Sisters of St. Paul live in communities. They are called according to the mystery of God's plan and are sent and brought together by providential circumstances. Strengthened at the source of divine love, their fraternal union should enable them to live more fully their life of consecration. Charity is intensified by a life of kindness, respect, patience, and mutual help in the service of God and of men.

sections.title: Mutual Support
sections.text: Fraternal life encourages openness toward others without loss of individuality. Communion of persons in charity presupposes mutual understanding. Consideration for others is disinterested; it embraces all, irrespective of office or ability. Special care is taken of the sisters who are advanced in age, disabled, sick, or who are undergoing trials. Community interchanges and silence foster encounter among the sisters: - Community interchange makes it possible for everyone to be accepted in the community, to express her own views and to hear those of others. It is an invitation to reflect on the fraternal spirit of the community. - Interior silence facilitates union with God and with others in God. It respects the mystery of divine action in the human heart. The relations within the community are simple, open and sincere. The sisters keep in mind that mutual trust is undermined by criticism and tale-bearing. In charity they strive towards unity despite difference in age, temperament, education and mentality. This diversity, causing as it does inevitable conflict, is also regarded as a source of mutual enrichment. Justice, based on respect for persons, allows for a certain amount of inequality, but the beneficiaries are careful to avoid all abuse. Growth of the Community

sections.title: Communication
sections.text: The community is a cell of the Mystical Body which is being continuously built up. Each sister brings to community life the best that is in her and accepts her sisters as they are. The gradual building-up of the community presupposes realism and patience to accept one another; hope to believe in the potentialities of each and all; courage to pardon and to love ever better in truth. Each sister is keenly aware of her involvement with all her sisters in the building-up and the growth of the community of which they are members. When the sister recognizes that she has publicly failed in charity, she asks pardon from the community. Life in Community

sections.title: Reconciliation
sections.text: Fraternal life calls for the sympathetic sharing of joys and sorrows, cares and difficulties, work and apostolate, with understanding and tact. It also calls for on-going communication. The community schedule is planned in accordance with the requirements of the apostolate. Certain outstanding moments deepen the communion of persons in charity: - Prayer in common unites minds and hearts in the praise of God. - Sharing meals at table is an opportunity for fraternal dialogue. - Periods of relaxation encourage free and spontaneous personal relationships and enable the sisters to help one another to preserve a joyful spirit. - Occasional projects enable all the sisters to cooperate in a common work. - Interchange in a friendly atmosphere helps the members of the community to know one another better and to see themselves and their apostolic life more clearly in the light of the Gospel. - The sisters live in their own religious house established according to Canon Law. Some part of the house is reserved for them. The permission of the local Superior is needed for every absence from the community. An absence of several days but not exceeding two months requires the permission of the Provincial Superior. The Superior General may grant a leave of absence for a longer period but not beyond one year except for reasons of health, studies or an apostolate undertaken in the name of the Institute (CC 665, 667, 608, 609). - A prudent discretion is called for in using the means of social communication (C 666). The living quarters of the sisters provide a favorable atmosphere for prayer, common life and personal life. Exterior silence is an important condition for rest and relaxation of tension. There are specified times and places of silence so as to foster prayer and reflection. The sisters obliged to live outside their community for study or apostolate go back to it to be renewed as soon as opportunity offers. Each sister and her competent Superiors study the frequency of her returns to the community. Apostolic Witness

sections.title: Hospitality
sections.text: The joy and fraternal courtesy prevailing among the sisters and their close cooperation in the fields of apostolate and work bear witness, in the Church and in the world, to the love of Christ in whose name the community is gathered. The setting in which the fraternal community exists is the Church where it works in coordination with the diocese and all parish organizations. The community is open to the needs of the world end, in all simplicity, endeavors to meet them. "Yaweh would speak with Moses face to face, as a man speaks with his friend." Ex 33:11 "God, you are my God, I am seeking you, my soul is thirsting for you my flesh is longing for you, a land parched, weary and waterless..." Ps 63:1 "In the morning, long before dawn, he got up and left the house, and went off to a lonely place and prayed there" Mk 1:35 "Say this when you pray: Father, may your name be held holy, your kingdom come." Lk 11:2 "I tell you solemnly once again, if two of you on earth agree to ask anything at all, it will be granted to you by my Father in heaven." Mt 18:19 "You should be awake, and praying not to be put to the test." Mt 26:41 "The proof that you are sons is that God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts: the Spirit that cries, 'Abba, Father.' " Ga 4:6 "All these joined in continuous prayer, together with several women, including Mary the mother of Jesus..." Ac 1:14 Life with God

sections.title: Life of Prayer
sections.text: God, who first loved us, carried out his plan to enter into a love relationship with man in spite of his sin. Jesus came to dwell among us to make known the Father. After his resurrection, he sent us the Holy Spirit who reveals to us the secrets of God. Our re-birth in Jesus Christ makes us enter into the divine intimacy and enables us to converse with God. Under the Impulse of the Holy Spirit

sections.title: The Eucharist
sections.text: Grace is life in God. Correspondence with the action of the Holy Spirit in us is the disposition fundamental to the interior life. The Spirit makes our prayer conform to that of Christ Jesus and enables us to offer the adoration, the praise, and the thanksgiving which are due to the Father. The Spirit disposes us to listen to the Word and gives us understanding of the divine mysteries. He creates in the heart an interior silence conducive to the longing for God or the quietude of a love that is fulfilled. Because the Spirit has been given us, we are witnesses and prophets, seeing the finger of God in all events. His presence in us is the source of contemplative and liturgical prayer. By Means of the Theological Virtues

sections.title: Eucharistic Adoration
sections.text: Life of union with God is founded on faith. She who believes relies completely on God and unites her will to the divine will. The prayer of a Christian, like that of Christ, is based on unconditional adherence to the designs of God. Hope awakens the desire for final reunion in the kingdom of heaven and prayer is a calling upon God who comes to save us. Charity animates prayer. When God manifests his love, he draws us to himself, inviting us to give ourselves completely. Through faith, hope, and charity a constant relationship is established with God. Moments of Renewal

sections.title: Liturgy of the Hours
sections.text: God, out of pure bounty, unites us to himself in love. The Lord is faithful and true; his love is eternal, but because of human frailty, special times must be set aside for God alone. These moments of renewal give new vigor to our love for God and ensure the authenticity of our apostolic charity. Spiritual Reading

sections.title: Mental Prayer
sections.text: "At various times in the past and in various different ways, God spoke to our ancestors through the prophets; but in our own time, the last days, he has spoken to us through his Son....". Only those who listen to the word of God and act on it bear fruit for eternal life. The Sisters of St. Paul draw from the Gospel the indispensable food for their Christian life. The reading of the epistles of the Apostle invites them to be imbued with the zeal of Paul who was on fire with the love of Christ and of men. The sisters receive the word of God with an attentive mind and a heart open to its call for conversion. Every day sufficient time is allotted to individual spiritual reading. When impeded, this obligation may be fulfilled by a minimum of two hours on a weekly basis. The schedule of the local community provides for common reading of the Book of Life on certain days. Contemplation

sections.title: Marian Devotion
sections.text: "Look, I am standing at the door, knocking. If one of you hears me calling and opens the door, I will come in to share his meal, side by side with him". Listening to the word of God prepares for encounter with the Lord in prayer. In silence and recollection, each sister is attentive to the mystery of God and remains in intimate communion with Christ. The Holy Spirit is the master of prayer life. He leads to greater conformity to Christ through the struggles and efforts of each day. Mental prayer is basically essential to prayer life. It is likewise a fruitful source of apostolate. The sisters make mental prayer in the morning and in the evening: - In the morning, it lasts at least one half hour; the time is decided in community. It may be deferred to another time only for a serious reason. - In the evening, a half hour of Eucharistic adoration is the occasion for offering the struggles of the day in union with the great offering of Christ to his Father. The monthly recollection which gives the sisters some hours for silence, reflection and prayer, and the annual retreat of eight days, as far as possible, afford time for prolonged prayer which contributes to a renewed outlook and a purified will. The short self-examination before God at noon helps the sister to see herself as she is and pick up strength to begin anew. The daily rosary and the angelus afford meditation with the Virgin Mary on the mysteries of Christ. Outside community prayer, the sister responds to grace inviting her to prolong her personal prayer, but without detriment to her professional task. Contemplation and Apostolate

sections.title: Sacred Scripture
sections.text: Attention to God in mental prayer helps us to see better the divine action in the world. The sisters, by their apostolic activity and the offering of their work, participate in the Redemption. Their love for their fellowmen is a sharing in God's love for all mankind. Thus, their life is unified: prayer animates action and the apostolate prolongs prayer and leads back to it. Houses for sisters who are retired or ill are places of more intensive prayer. The sisters who are suffering and deprived of the joys of the direct apostolate are, in a special manner, living in union with Christ in his saving Passion and are a source of strength for the sisters in the apostolic field. Liturgical Life

sections.title: Retreats
sections.text: "They went as a body to the Temple every day but met in their houses for the breaking of bread; .... they praised God and were looked up to by everyone." The liturgy is prayer and action of Christ living in the Church. When possible, the Sisters of St. Paul take active part in the liturgical celebrations of the parish communities to which they belong. The holy sacrifice of the Mass, perfect praise and source of grace, is the center of their life. Each day, the sisters participate in the Eucharistic Sacrifice of Christ offering himself to the Father for the redemption of the world. Lauds, Vespers and Compline bring together at the appropriate time the members of the community to praise God with one voice. This is the praise of the Church lifting up to the Father the thanksgiving and the longings of mankind. The Sacrament of Reconciliation is an act of Christ which renews or strengthens our covenant with God and with the members of his People. Whenever the sisters receive it with faith, they allow God's glory to manifest itself in the exercise of his mercy. The sisters draw up the schedule of their prayer life in community. Any hindrances and dispensations are studied with the Superior. When the community gathers for prayer, it fulfills this function in the name of all its members; so, when a sister happens to be prevented by some pressing task, she does not have to take up that part of the Office which she missed. The community may be deprived of Holy Mass by the prevailing circumstances. If so, a celebration may be held as a substitute. Individual cases call for prolonged private prayer. A mission post having no priest may be accepted, but this service to the Church necessitates the regular replacement of the sisters. Prayers for the Dead

sections.title: Days of Recollection
sections.text: The members of the Congregation remain united beyond death through the Communion of Saints. The Sisters of St. Paul remember in prayer their deceased sisters and recommend them to God in the course of the liturgy. When notice of a sister's death is received, at least one Mass is offered in each Provincial House and all the sisters offer to God the Eucharistic Sacrifice in which they participate. These suffrages are doubled in the whole Congregation for the Sovereign Pontiff, the Superiors General and, in the Provinces, for the Bishops and the Provincials. During each annual retreat a Mass is celebrated for all the deceased sisters. Once a year, a Mass is said in every house for deceased relatives and benefactors. "As the Father sent me, so am I sending you" Jn 20:21 "I am the vine, you are the branches. Whoever remains in me, with me in him, bears fruit in plenty; for cut off from me you can do nothing." Jn 15:5 "If anyone declares himself for me in the presence of men, I will declare myself for him in the presence of my Father in heaven." Mt 10:32 "Life to me is not a thing to waste words on, provided that when I finish my race I have carried out the mission the Lord Jesus gave me and that was to bear witness to the Good News of God's grace." Ac 20:24 "As for me, brothers, when I came to you, it was not with any show of oratory or philosophy, but simply to tell you what God had guaranteed. During my stay with you, the only knowledge I claimed to have was about Jesus, and only about him as the crucified Christ."

sections.title: Apostolic Mission
sections.text: The Sisters of St. Paul share in the apostolic mission of the Church. Consecrated to God, they live and work among men, eager to announce the Good News to all. Consecration by its very nature has apostolic influence. The love that inspires the gift of one's life to God is dynamic; it makes of the consecrated person a witness to divine grace. Consecration gives a special characteristic to the witnessing of religious: among the People of God, they announce the future kingdom. The charism of consecration is given for the Church and for the world. (C673)

sections.title: Preferential Option
sections.text: Through grace the apostle cooperates in the mission of the Son. She lives in close union with her Lord whose face she recognizes and contemplates in all those whom she meets. The apostle marvels at the respect God has for human liberty, his divine patience, and the workings of grace. Filled with wonder at the transforming action of the Spirit in the hearts of men, she praises and thanks the Father of Light from whom comes every perfect gift. Teaching of St. Paul

sections.title: Works of Mercy
sections.text: The apostolic life of the sisters draws its inspiration from the life and teaching of St. Paul. The apostle is God's messenger. Aware of her own indigence and the greatness of her mission, she is open to the Spirit who alone can touch the human heart. The apostle, following in the footsteps of Christ, is spurred on by charity and is ready to suffer all for him who overcame death through the humiliation of the cross. With steadfast faith and firm hope, she goes ahead in spite of obstacles and never tires of announcing Jesus Christ. The apostle is available to all without distinction. She adopts the language and adjusts herself to the culture and customs of different peoples or of different social environment. By preference, she attend to the most needy and underprivileged, realizing that the lack of knowledge or understanding of God is the greatest misfortune of all. A life wholly Apostolic

sections.title: Education Ministry
sections.text: The sister's whole life is apostolic. Each one bears witness to Christ by what she is. Consecration lived in faith and charity, free from pettiness and rigidity, radiates the joy of complete self-giving to God. The community, united in charity, announces Christ and arouses the desire to know him. The Sisters of St. Paul follow the Master who came not to be served but to serve, and their whole life attitude is Gospel-oriented. By their living faith and boundless charity they make known to others God's love and challenge them to a response. The sisters work in cooperation with all, respecting the rights of each, and have real concern for the good of persons. Their professional competence and the quality of their habitual or occasional relationships have repercussions on their apostolic action. The sisters recognize and heed the signs of God in the world. They have at heart the salvation of all their fellowmen whose call they hear and try to answer with discernment and generosity. The sisters sent by the Congregation know that they can rely on the support of the prayers of all the members. No matter what kind of service may be entrusted to them, they always act as Sisters of St. Paul. By living her consecration to the full, in health as in sickness, every sister, regardless of her occupation, announces the kingdom and makes it present among her fellowmen. To enhance the human and spiritual quality of presence to her community and to the world, the sister constantly seeks to keep her life unified. She takes time for renewing her spiritual and physical energies, and is willing to limit her sphere of action when she is inclined to become over-involved. Apostolate and Adaptation

sections.title: Healthcare Ministry
sections.text: Continuous adaptation is a concern of the Congregation. Superiors and sisters listen to the plea of the Church expressed by the hierarchy and endeavor to respond in line with their own specific purpose. The present works as well as the new foundations should meet contemporary needs. It is therefore advisable to be alert to the requirements of evangelization and local needs. The innovations or the readjustements required for a better adaptation to times, places, and persons call for a change of mentality. These often entail sacrifices which renew the generosity of apostolic enthusiasm. The Sister of St. Paul adjusts herself to her environment; she seeks to promote the greater good of each person. She is creative in her efforts to give better education and care. Striving to live in the spirit of the Beatitudes, her concern is the development of the underprivileged. In an attitude of deep respect for those to whom they are sent, the sisters learn to appreciate the specific values of all peoples. They have respect for the freedom of each individual, while endeavoring to bring them closer to the light of the Gospel. Apostolate in the Church

sections.title: Apostolic Availability
sections.text: The sisters help one another and unite their efforts in the apostolate. They work with the laity in a spirit of mutual understanding and follow the directives of the hierarchy (C. 678). The sisters do not undertake a task or a function outside of the Institute without the permission of their lawful Superior (C. 671). Sent by the Church through their Superiors, the sisters participate in the work of salvation entrusted by the Christ to his Church: "Go, therefore, make disciples of all the nations..." Like the Apostle, the sisters too, while wholly dedicated to their task, are nevertheless concerned about all the Churches. They seek ways of remaining united to their sisters in the far-off missions. Whenever it becomes impossible to announce the Gospel openly, the whole life of the consecrated person announces that God exists and that he loves us. All through her life and in all circumstances, the Sister of St. Paul, confident of the Lord's victory, even when exposed to contradiction, radiates a joy that is serene and a hope that is invincible. "... Yes, as the clay is in the potter's hand, so you are in mine, House of Israel." Jr 18:6 "When you seek me you shall find me, when you seek me with all your heart." Jr 29:13 "Because of Christ, I have come to consider all these advantage that I had as disadvantages. Not only that, but I believe nothing can happen that will outweigh the supreme advantage of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord. For him I have accepted the loss of everything, and I look on everything as so much rubbish if only I can have Christ... Not that I have become perfect yet; I have not yet won, but I am still running, trying to capture the prize for which Christ Jesus captured me." Ph 3:7-12 "Out of his infinite glory, may he (the Father) give you the power through his Spirit for your hidden self to grow strong, so that Christ may live in your hearts through faith and then planted in love and built on love ..." Ep 3:16-17 "Seeing the crowds, he went up the hill. There he sat down and was joined by his disciples. Then he began to speak. This is what he taught them..." Mt 5:1-2 Grace and Responsibility

sections.title: Gift of Fidelity
sections.text: The People of God is on the march in response to the call of the Lord. While on this pilgrimage we are called to cooperation with the divine action and to mutual assistance. The Lord gives us the opportunity of participating freely in his work, and makes us responsible for one another. Moreover, all the Sisters of St. Paul should know that, as far as they are concerned, they are responsible for the vitality of consecrated life in the Church and in their Congregation. The Holy Spirit never ceases to inspire new vocations to consecrated life in the Church. These emerging vocations need to see the witness to charity given by each sister and by the community as a whole.

sections.title: Growth in Fidelity
sections.text: Persons intending to serve God and neighbor in the Congregation of the Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres should be filled with a sincere, realistic, and supernatural desire for apostolic religious life according to the Gospel. Their life ideal is "to give themselves to God for the good of the Church and the service of their fellowmen". During the time of probation they examine their motivation and all through life, sustained by prayer, they remain faithful to the grace of their initial call. Admission

sections.title: Call to Conversion
sections.text: When admitting postulants, the competent Superiors see to it that the candidates have sufficient health to undertake the service of the poor and that they have reached genuine maturity of mind. According to Canon Law (CC 642-645), the postulants must be free from all impediments. They must also have belonged to the Catholic religion for at least three years. Postulancy

sections.title: Renewal of Vows
sections.text: The aim of the postulancy is to initiate the candidates into the life-style and work of the Congregation, to examine their aptitudes and motivations, and to prepare them for the novitiate. During the postulancy which lasts at least six months and at most one year, fundamentals of doctrine help the postulants to deepen their prayer life. Study of the history of the Congregation initiates them into the life of the Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres. Novitiate

sections.title: Sacrament of Reconciliation
sections.text: The aim of the novitiate is formation in religious life: conversion of heart and growth in Christ. From the time of her entrance into the novitiate, the novice follows Christ in the Gospel. She gradually discovers the demands of her vocation and the meaning of her consecration. Open to the invitation of the Spirit, she learns to encounter Christ Jesus in Sacred Scripture, prayer, the Eucharist, community life, and in all events. She likewise discovers the meaning of the mission of a Sister of St. Paul in the history and the life of the Congregation and also in the apostolic contacts and the activities which are the object of team-work and research in community (C 652). Before admission to profession it is to be ascertained that the conditions laid down by Canon Law are fulfilled (C 656) The Novitiate lasts one year, at most two years. It takes place in the novitiate house which must provide the atmosphere of silence and recollection absolutely necessary during this period of initiation to religious life. For a serious reason, the novitiate may be prolonged for six months beyond the two years. The novice keeps in touch with the Directress of Novices and returns to the novitiate house two months before profession. During the twelve canonical months, absences from the novitiate house exceeding three months, whether continuous or with interruption, render the novitiate invalid. An absence of more than fifteen days should be made up for. Through courses in theology and Scripture, participation in the liturgy, study of the Book of Life, and a deeper knowledge of the spiritual life, the novice progresses gradually toward her first commitment. When she has finished her period of probation, the novice may, with the agreement of the Directress of Novices, apply to her Major Superior for admission to profession. This presupposes that the applicant has the necessary dispositions and is at least twenty years of age. The Provincial Superior or, in her stead, the Directress of Novices, may authorize a novice in danger of death to make her vows, omitting all reference to duration. If the novice recovers, her status will be the same as if she had not made profession. The novices have the right to the same suffrages as the professed. Juniorate

sections.title: Spiritual Direction
sections.text: Formation does not end with temporary profession. During her years in the juniorate, the young religious must be helped to unify her life. She learns by experience to combine love of God with apostolic zeal, duty of state with universal charity, prayer with life. She is helped by the Directress of the Juniorate but it is desirable what each sister gradually assume responsibility for her own formation. The juniorate covers the whole period of temporary profession. It normally lasts five years but may be extended to seven or reduced to three years by the decision of the Superior General with the consent of her Council. Before admission to perpetual profession the conditions enumerated by Canon Law are to be verified as fulfilled (CC 658, 689). During the juniorate, the Provinces provide for at least one year of doctrinal formation at the most convenient time. The professional formation varies according to the individuals, but the actual experiences in the apostolate should cover a minimum of one year before perpetual profession. Temporary profession is annual for a period of five years, but after three years the sister may commit herself for two years if she wishes to do so. At the end of their juniorate the junior sisters address a written request to their Major Superior for admission to perpetual profession, and prepare for this definitive act of commitment during a period of at least two months. The sisters of temporary vows may participate in the consultations made in their own Province, but they can neither vote nor be voted for. Persons in Charge of Formation

sections.title: Ongoing Formation
sections.text: All the sisters take an interest in the question of formation, so as to better understand what is being done in this respect and to cooperate in a positive manner. Thus, it will be easier for them to enter into dialogue with their young sisters, especially when the time comes for the latter to adjust to community life and to participate in the work and the apostolate. Formation should take into account the different mentalities and the particular apostolic needs of each country or region. The Directress of Novices is a perpetually professed sister entrusted with the responsibility of forming the novices and guiding them to first profession. She is appointed by the Superior General with the consent of her Council (C 651). She must be at least thirty years of age and have sufficient experience in religious life. The Superior General and her Council are responsible for formation in the Congregation; in the Provinces, the Provincial Superior and her Council are responsible. An Assistant General keeps in contact with the Directresses of Formation in the Provinces and Districts, and has a genuine concern for unity. Meetings of all those in charge of formation in the Congregation are desirable. The Provinces attend to the preparation and regular replacement of the Directresses of Formation. The Directress of Postulants prepares them gradually for the novitiate. The Directress of Juniors is appointed by the Superior General with the consent of her Council. She is responsible for guiding the Junior Sisters towards perpetual profession and for helping them adjust to life in the communities. Frequent contacts are indispensable among those in charge of formation. Local Superiors entrusted with sisters of temporary vows maintain regular contact with the Directress of the Juniorate. On-going formation

sections.title: Initial Formation
sections.text: Life is a long experience of the fidelity of God to which corresponds a desire for greater personal fidelity. It is the work of grace in the human heart. A period of recollection should accompany each stage of our life. This pause is a help toward greater awareness of the exigencies of the love of God and fellowman in view of a more generous response. Each Province organizes spiritual renewal periods lasting one or several months for the sisters who have five, ten, twenty-five years of perpetual profession. These programs are to be oriented toward a renewed awareness of the demands of religious consecration. Moreover, a sister may ask for a spiritual month or a personal retreat if she feels a real need for it. On the general level of the Congregation, periods of spiritual renewal are organized. They are oriented toward a deeper understanding of the spirit of the Congregation and provide opportunities for encounter on an international level which brings about increased unity among the sisters.

sections.title: Novitiate
sections.text: The formation of Superiors is highly important. It is an on-going process. The Provincial Council takes the necessary steps to ensure this formation. The missionaries receive a solid formation in doctrine as well as good professional training. They are to be given sufficient time to study the language, the culture and the traditions of the people to whom they are sent. A return to their native land is also an opportunity for spiritual and apostolic renewal.

sections.title: Postulancy
sections.text: On the professional plane, continuous updating is essential. Information and documentary material serve to arouse interest in economic, social and political problems. The Superiors attend to this, and all the sisters are eager for a better knowledge of the contemporary world. While they do not neglect knowledge and technique, they are not to forget that their dealings with the world in the spirit of the Gospel require a humble and generous heart ready to suffer all for the coming of God's kingdom (C 661). The community provides the sisters with books designed to nourish the life of faith, and with works or periodicals of general and professional culture. Superiors and Provincial Chapters seek earnestly to devise new activities for those sisters who, having reached the age limit, have to retire from regular service. Fulfillment

sections.title: Aspirancy
sections.text: At the close of our earthly life we shall return to God, making the supreme act of obedience whereby the adopted son is identified with the well-beloved Son. If Christ is our life, to die will finally be a gain, since this death will fulfill our desire to be with Christ forever. All through our life, this death is being realized and prepared for in the numerous forms of renunciation whether voluntarily embraced or simply endured. Separation from the Institute

sections.title: Formators
sections.text: When vigilance weakens, the meaning of the vocation tends to grow vague, with the result that separation from the Institute is sometimes envisaged. A sister of temporary vows may, for a grave reason, ask for an indult to leave, and the Superior General who may grant it with the consent of her Council (C 688). The request for exclaustration made by a sister of perpetual vows is addressed to the Superior General who may grant it with the consent of her Council, but not for more than three years (CC 686, 687). For very grave reasons maturely weighed before God, the request for secularization made by a sister of perpetual vows is addressed to the Superior General who forwards it to the Holy See with her opinion and that of her Council (C 691). When the dismissal of a sister of temporary or perpetual profession is judged necessary, after serious study of the case and the decision of the Superior General and her Council, the procedure fixed by Canon Law shall be followed (CC 694-703). Sisters who lawfully leave or are lawfully dismissed from the Congregation cannot claim anything for any work done in the Institute. The Congregation will observe equity and evangelical charity towards the separated member (C 702).

sections.title: Formation Community
sections.text: The admission of a perpetually professed sister coming from another Institute requires the authorization of the Superior General of both Institutes, with the consent of their respective Councils. A probation of three years should precede the profession of the sister. If the sister refuses to make this profession or if she is not accepted, she either returns to her former Institute or obtains an indult of secularization (C 684). Re-admission to the Institute

sections.title: Formation Program
sections.text: The sister who legitimately left the Institute after having completed her novitiate or after having made profession may be re-admitted by the Superior General with the consent of her Council without having to repeat the novitiate. The Superior General is to determine the appropriate length of the period of probation before temporary profession as well as the duration of the vows prior to perpetual profession (CC 655, 657). "After the meal Jesus said to Simon Peter, 'Simon son of John, do you love me more than these others do?' He answered, 'Yes Lord, you know I love you'. Jesus said to him, 'Feed my lambs'." Jn 21:15 "You call me Master and Lord, and rightly; so I am. If I, then, the Lord and Master, have washed your feet, you should wash each other's feet. I have given you an example so that you may copy what I have done to you." Jn 13:13-15 "Be on your guard for yourselves and for all the flock of which the Holy Spirit has made you the overseers, to feed the Church of God which he bought with his own blood." Ac 20:28 "Proclaim the message and, welcome or unwelcome, insist on it. Refute falsehood, correct error, call to obedience- but do all with patience and with the intention of teaching... Be careful always to choose the right course; be brave under trials; make the preaching of the Good News your life's work, in thoroughgoing service."

sections.title: Unity in Charity
sections.text: God, the Lord and Master of the universe, created man. He bestowed on him the privilege to rule over creation and bring it to fulfillment; he also endowed him with the liberty to acknowledge the authority of his God and Father. Sin had upset this balance and God's only Son came to teach men the dignity and the liberty of the redeemed in submission to the authority of their heavenly Father. Christ has been vested with power and glory from above because of the fidelity of his obedience. He is both Lord and perfect Servant. Jesus, Servant and Lord

sections.title: Bond of Love
sections.text: All through the Gospel, Christ's main concern is to accomplish the Father's will which he seeks in the particular circumstances of his life, in the events and persons that he never rejects. If he speaks with authority, it is because his whole life is in harmony with his teaching. He whom the apostles called Master is above all the Good Master. He welcomes all those who come to him, without distinction. His apostles are not servants but friends, and Christ continues to trust Peter even after his denial. Not only do we recognize Jesus as the Master waiting on his servants, but we see him in person washing the feet of his friends before giving them the bread of his love. In the Church, the exercise of authority draws its inspiration from the life of Christ Jesus. Obedience, Bond of Unity

sections.title: Unity in Diversity
sections.text: The Sisters of St. Paul, by their profession of obedience, promise to live fully the faith of their baptism. They consider the life of obedience, as proposed by the Congregation, to be for them the best way to seek and accomplish the will of God, in the service of their fellowmen. Their obedience animated by charity is the bond of their unity. Through the obedience of all, an Institute of apostolic life preserves its unity of decision and action, notwithstanding the dispersion of its members which zeal for the reign of God necessarily entails. In the Congregation, all those appointed to serve as Superiors must be firmly grounded in a deep supernatural faith. Their task calls for discernment according to God as well as an overflowing charity in which all may discover an aspect of God's love for men. The apostolic objective of the Congregation cannot be achieved unless all the sisters are sincerely united with the Superior General.

sections.title: Communion
sections.text: In the Congregation of the Sisters of St. Paul, the Superiors on all levels - general, provincial, local - endeavor to stimulate effective cooperation on the part of their Council or other bodies formed for this purpose. Moreover, a living spirit should bind together the different structural levels of the Institute: general, provincial and local. Lastly, there should be continuous communication between the Superiors and the sisters. In this way everybody is better informed when faced with decisions to be made and applied. The Superior General

sections.title: Collaboration
sections.text: The Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres recognize in their Superior General the person whom God has entrusted with the direction of the Congregation. They trust and respect her and are united through obedience to her directives. The Superior General is commissioned by the Church to govern the Congregation. She shares in a special way in the gift and grace of the origins of the Congregation. She is the guarantor of the fidelity of her sisters and of the authenticity of their mission. The authority of the Superior General is not derived from the General Chapter which elects her, but from God through the ministry of the Church which approved the Congregation and continues to recognize it. This authority finds its meaning in the Gospel: "Anyone who listens to you listens to me". It is a service in imitation of Christ the Servant. The first duty of the Superior General is to carry out her mission and to assume her responsibilities according to universal and proper law. She is open to the Holy Spirit, attentive to the needs of the Church and the world, while seeking to promote the religious and apostolic élan of the Congregation according to its aim and spirit. For a more effective service in the spreading of God's kingdom, the Superior General sets before the Provinces the priority needs of the mission. She has authority over all the Provinces and Districts, the local houses and the members of the Congregation. The Provincial or District Superiors are appointed by the Superior General and cooperate with her in the government of the Congregation in a relationship of obedience. Mode of Government

sections.title: Communion with Church
sections.text: As servant of all her sisters, the Superior General has a persevering interest in each one. Sisterly and attentive, simple and discreet, she is careful to keep up contact through personal visits, letters and circulars. In her relations with the sisters, she is kind, understanding, encouraging, and yet really firm in her respect for the obligations of consecrated life and fidelity to the Constitutions. In the interests of the Church, the Superior General endeavors to develop the apostolate of the Congregation. After the example of St. Paul, an ardent zeal for the Gospel of Jesus Christ inspires all her acts. The Superior General needs to acquire a thorough knowledge of the Congregation. She keeps informs personally as well as through the intermediary of her Assistants and the Provincial or district Superiors; reflection made, she gives her opinion on the affairs of each Province. Finally, prayer and union with God are of prime importance for the Superior General. They are vital to the discernment which she must practice for the general welfare and the glory of God, in great fidelity to the spirit of the Congregation. The vigilance of the Superior General also extends to the administration of the temporal goods. She represents the Congregation, sign the acts passed in the name of the Institute and may authorize expenditures to the amount of her financial capacity.

sections.title: Ecumenical Spirit
sections.text: The resignation of the Superior General during her term of office must be referred to the Holy See. In case of cessation of office on the part of the Superior General, the first Assistant, with the help of the other Councilors, takes over the government of the Congregation, but within the following six months she convokes the General Chapter. Superior General and Assistants General

sections.title: Government Structure
sections.text: The Superior General and Assistants General form a community of prayer and reflection in order to promote the spiritual and apostolic good of the Congregation. The Superior General, with her Assistants, sets the objectives to be met within a specified time and together they schedule their visits to the Provinces. In the course of these visits, the Assistants ensure a real bond between the Superior General and each Province. They also encourage unity among the sisters and with their immediate Superior. On their return, they give the Superior General and the Council an exact report of their visit relative to the mission entrusted to them. As the close associates of the Superior General, the Assistants discreetly help her in her functions. They present their views and suggestions in a devoted and disinterested spirit. The four Assistants General are elected by the General Chapter for six years and are eligible for reelection. In case of resignation, of disability due to illhealth or the death of an Assistant General, the General Council provides for her replacement until the next Chapter. The General Council

sections.title: Superior General
sections.text: The Assistants General make up the General Council, whose mission is to enlighten the Superior General, help her in her task and cooperate with her toward the good of the Congregation. The Council, presided over by the Superior General meet as often as necessary, but at least once a month. The agenda of the Council meeting is prepared by the Superior General and given to the Assistants who acquaint themselves with the information and requests of the Provinces, or study the questions proposed by the Superior General. The Assistants General contribute to discernment by giving their advice in all freedom. They work in a climate of openness, since cooperation and submission to the final decision. The Provincial Superiors and their Assistants or the Bursar General may be called to the Council sessions. They have no right to vote, neither does the Secretary General, unless the Council decides otherwise in well-defined and provisional case. The General Council acts as a college over which the Superior General presides in such serious cases as the dismissal of a professed sister and the discharge or resignation of the Superior from office. These cases are decided by a majority vote. The General Council also acts as Council with a deliberative vote. In this case the Assistants vote on the proposal of the Superior General. If the vote is negative, the Superior cannot act but she may propose another solution. Finally, the Superior may request a consultative vote, in which case she remains free to act in all prudence, according to her conscience.

sections.title: Election of Superior General
sections.text: Question Requiring the Deliberative Vote of the General Council: Creation of new Provinces (C 681) Appointment of the Secretary General and of the Bursar General Appointment of Provincial Superiors and Provincial Assistants Admission to perpetual profession Admission of novices to first profession Anticipation by two years or prolongation for two years of the ordinary period of temporary profession Re-admission of a sister who has already made her novitiate or profession in Congregation (C 690) Transfer of a perpetually professed sister to another religious Institute (CC 684-685) Admission to the novitiate of a candidate who had been admitted to another Institute of consecrated life or to a society of apostolic life (C 645) Appointment of District Superior and their Councilors Appointment of Regional Superior Appointment of Directresses of Formation Maintaining of a local Superior in office for a third or a fourth term Opening of houses with the written consent of the diocesan bishop (C609) Closing of houses after consultation with the diocesan bishop(C 616) Erection or transfer of a novitiate Transfer of the Generalate after consultation with the Provincial Superior; the Holy See is informed of the transfer Approval or transfer of a Provincial House Authorization for loans, alienations, debts to be contracted and contacts made in the name of the Congregation Authorization for expenditures in excess of what Provincial or District Councils are allowed Authorization for a sister of temporary profession to leave the Institute before the expiration of her vows (C 688) Authorization for a novice to make her novitiate in a house of the Congregation other than the novitiate house (C 647) Consultative Advice: Decision as to where the General Chapter and the Council of Congregation are to be held Preparation and convocation of the General Chapter - ordinary or extraordinary. * * *

sections.title: Term of Superior General
sections.text: The Superior General may authorize a professed sister to stay outside the Institute, in the limits established by Canon Law (C 665) The Superior General, with the advice of her Council, may delegate to the Provincial Superior, the faculties for: the modification of wills and the renunciation of patrimonial goods. The Superior General and her Council readjust periodically the amount of each Provincial Superior's financial capacity, when acting alone or with her Council. The report of the General Council meetings drawn up by the Secretary General, is approved and signed by the members of the Council. Secretary General - Bursar General

sections.title: Duties of Superior General
sections.text: The Superior General, assisted by her Council, chooses, among or outside its members, perpetually professed sisters to fulfill the function of Secretary General and Bursar General. The Superior General brings valuable and effective assistance to the work of the Superior General and the Council. She carries out her duties with discretion, attends the meetings of the General Council and keeps the minutes. She is responsible for the updating of information and statistics which help to give a clear picture of the life of the Congregation. The Bursar General administers the goods of the Congregation under the responsibility and control of the Superior General and the Council. She accomplishers her task with competence and integrity; she manages the property of the poor. Every six months she presents the accounts of the General Administration to the Council for examination and approval. Every year she receives the financial reports of the Provinces and prepares the accounts in view of the General Chapter. Administration of Temporal Goods

sections.title: General Council
sections.text: Insofar as they are juridical persons, the Congregation, the Provinces and the houses are capable of acquiring, possessing, administering and alienating temporal goods. The exercise of this capacity shall conform to the prescribed law of the Church and that of the respective country where the Congregation is established. Those responsible for management bear in mind that their way of conducting business affairs involves not only their own personal reputation but also that of the whole Congregation and even that of the Church. The Superior General, with the consent of her Council, may authorize loans and alienations within the limits set by the Holy See whose permission is required for amounts above this sum. This permission is equally necessary in transactions concerning goods donated to the Church in virtue of a vow or objects which are precious by reason of their artistic or historical value (C 638) The Congregation is not liable for debts contracted by a sister without the authorization of the lawful Superiors. As far as possible, the management of goods and the accounting system will be identical in each Province. The Provincial Superior

sections.title: General Councilors
sections.text: The Provincial Superior is a Major Superior entrusted by the Superior General with the care of a Province. In a relationship of obedience, she acts in union with the Superior General, faithful to the directives of the Church, the Book of Life and Chapter resolutions. The Provincial Superior must have ten years of perpetual profession and be forty years of age. She is appointed by the Superior General with the consent of her Council after consultation with the professed sisters of the Province for a first term of five years, renewable once. She may be maintained in office for a third term if two-thirds of the consultation is in her favor. She may not hold any other office during her term. With her appointment as Provincial, she receives mission to animate the spiritual and apostolic life of her sisters within the bounds of her Province. The Provincial Superior confides to the sister their respective mission in the work of spreading God's reign. She does not allow herself to be influenced by human views but consults and prays in order to discern the will of God for her sisters. She respects the responsibilities she gives to each person and to the local Superiors in particular. Keeping in mind the directives of the bishop and the needs of the poor, the Provincial Superior studies and evaluates the communities founded in her Province with a view to giving better service to the Church and the world. Any new plans are presents to the Superior General who, with her Council, takes the decision deemed advisable. The Provincial Superior has the important duty to visit regularly each house in her Province. She gives renewed impetus to the spiritual and apostolic life of the sisters, upholds and encourages the local Superiors in the fulfillment of their duty and does not overlook the material aspects of the sisters' lives. The Provincial Superior organizes retreats and periods of spiritual renewal for her Province. She attends to the on-going doctrinal, intellectual and professional formation of the sisters. With a view to a more effective apostolate, she designates, for specialized studies such persons as have the aptitude. The Provincial Superior sees to the implementation of the resolutions of the Chapters or of the decisions of the Superior General and her Council. She keeps her sisters informed about the life of the Province and the Congregation, and fosters mutual help among the local communities.

sections.title: Election of Councilors
sections.text: Each Province has the mission of the Church at heart, and while the Provincial Superior urges the sisters to pray continually for vacations, she herself strives to make known the meaning of the consecrated life. Every year, in accordance with the spirit of the Congregation, the Provincial Superior makes available to the Superior General the prospective missionaries among the sisters. Any sojourn, momentary or definitive, of a sister in another Province or abroad, is submitted to the Superior General. The Provincial Superior: Admits postulants after having the required information. Receives the vows of the sisters of her Province, either in person or through a sister delegated by her. May allow the anticipation of first profession, but not by more than fifteen days. May authorize a professed sister to sojourn outside the Institute; however not more than two months. Initiates process for the dismissal of a professed sister if she judges it proper after having consulted her Council ( C697; cf BL Art. 67).
