Authorizes expenditures to the amount of her financial capacity. Carefully watches over the administration of the temporal goods of her Province. May authorize the publication of writings on matters of religion or morals (C 832). Attitude of the Provincial Superior

sections.title: Council Meetings
sections.text: The Provincial Superior continually seeks the will of God in prayer. Through union with God she finds the strength to sustain her sisters and the serenity of mind and heart indispensable in overcoming difficulties. The Provincial Superior is faithful to the thinking of the Church. So, she expects her sisters to have the same fidelity to ecclesial teaching. The relationship between the Provincial Superior and the sisters is based on trust and discretion. Such an atmosphere enables all to assume their duty in peace and joyful liberty. This trust on the part of the Provincial Superior does not dispense with vigilance. The Provincial Superior is steadfast in her efforts to bring about one mind, spirit and heart in the Province. This unity of persons in God makes it possible to reconcile all inevitable conflicting viewpoints Finally, the Provincial Superior maintains close contact with the Superior General and communicates with her frequently in all trust and openness. The Provincial Superior and the Province Assistants

sections.title: Provincial Superior
sections.text: The Assistants help the Provincial Superior by discreet and loyal cooperation. Owing to diversity of their qualifications, they contribute to the Provincial Council the fruit of their experience and observation so as to better animate the Province and realize a more effective service of the poor. The Provincial Assistants are appointed by the Superior General and her Council, after consultation with the Provincial Superior and the professed sisters of the Province. Their term of office is the same as that of the Provincial Superior and is renewable. The Provincial Assistants are four in number, among whom may be chosen the Secretary and the Bursar of the Province. If the Province is divided into Regions, the number of Assistance will depend upon the size of the Province. The number will be determined by agreement with the Superior General. The Superior General and her Council provide for the replacement of an Assistant in case of death or major impediment. The Provincial Council

sections.title: Provincial Council
sections.text: The mission of the Provincial Council is to help the Provincial Superior in her task as spiritual and apostolic leader of the Province. Together with the Provincial Superior and under her responsibility, the Provincial Council studies the directives and suggestions of the Superior General and her Council. It also studies the apostolic needs of the Province and the means of assuring the religious and professional formation of the sisters. The agenda of the Council meeting is prepared by the Provincial Superior and given to the Assistants who may also bring an issue before the Council Whatever the opinion freely advanced by one Assistant or another, they all rally to the final decision in a great spirit of unity. The Directresses of Formation are convened and listened to in meetings that deal with the admission either to the novitiate or the profession. The Provincial Bursar is called when the accounts are examined. Sometimes one or several local Superiors or sisters may be called to the Provincial Council to clarify some issue; however, none of them have right of vote.

sections.title: Provincial Duties
sections.text: The Provincial Council acts trough a deliberative or a consultative vote. Certain questions require the decision of the Superior General and her Council. Matters Requiring the Decision of the Superior General with the Consent of her Council The presentation of these matters by the Provincial Superior presupposes the previous consent of her own Council: Admission or re-admission, according to Canon Law, of a sister who has already made novitiate or her temporary or perpetual profession in the Congregation or in Institute. Admission to first profession Prolongation of the period of the novitiate or of the period of temporary vows Admission to perpetual profession Appointment of Directresses of Formation Retaining of a local Superior in office for a third term and beyond, according to Canon Law Authorization to incur expenses in excess of what the Provincial Council is allowed Erection or transfer of a novitiate Erection and suppression of houses with the authorization of the diocesan bishop Change of apostolic orientation of existing houses with the consent of the diocesan bishop (C 612) Deliberative Vote of the Provincial Council Admission to the novitiate Dismissal of a novice Admission to renewal of vows Appointment of the Secretary and the Bursar for the Province Appointment of local Superiors Renewal of local Superiors for a second term of office Approval of the accounts of the Provincial Bursar Exercise of faculties delegated by the Superior General regarding renunciation of patrimonial goods or modification of wills. Consultative Vote of the Provincial Council Anticipating new assignments Fixing the date and place of the Provincial Chapter and the Council of Province Preparing and convoking the Provincial Chapter and the Council of Province. The Secretary and the Bursar of the Province

sections.title: Local Superior
sections.text: The Provincial Secretary draws up the minutes of the Province Council meetings, keeps the registers of the Province, is in charge of the archives and keeps the chronicles updated. She gives discreet and disinterested assistance to the Provincial Superior and her Council. With real concern for the common good, the Provincial Bursar administers the goods of the Province under the direction of the Provincial Superior and her Council. She receives the contributions of the houses, and according to the available funds, shares in the financial burden of the Congregation by sending funds to the general treasury. The Secretary and the Bursar of the province are appointed by the Provincial Superior and her Council. The Provincial Bursar examines the accounts of the local houses and every six months she presents her books the Provincial Superior and to the Council. Every year, after approval by the Council, she sends to the Superior General a report on the financial situation of the Province. Administration of Temporal Goods

sections.title: Local Community
sections.text: The Provincial Superior, in person or through another, makes sure that the books of account are properly kept, and that the inventory of the movable property of the Congregation is updated in the houses which do not belong to the Congregation. She sees to it that the conditions stipulated in deeds of donation or foundation are faithfully respected. The dowry capital is administered from the residence of the Major Superior. The dowry becomes the property of the Congregation only on the death of the professed sister whether of temporary or perpetual vows. The revenues belong by right to the Congregation. The Provincial Superior and her Council determine for local houses those cases where extraordinary expenditures require prior authorization. The District Superior

sections.title: Community Meetings
sections.text: The District Superior is responsible for several communities which form a unity destined to develop into a Province. She is appointed by the Superior General and her Council after consultation with the sisters of the District. She must have five years of perpetual profession. The duration of her term of office is three years, twice renewable. The District Superior exercises authority delegated by the Superior General. She is assisted by a Council composed of two to four members whose term of office is the same as her own, but renewable.

sections.title: General Chapter
sections.text: The mission of the District Superior is to assure the spiritual animation of the communities of the District, to provide for the formation of the new members, organize the annual retreats, foster the apostolic élan and visit the houses. Periodically, the District Superior informs the Superior General about the life of the District. After consulting her Council the District Superior. Admits postulants Admits to renewal of temporary vows Decides on changes of assignment for the sisters and informs the Superior General Authorizes expenses within the limits of her financial capacity Manages the District funds Studies the possibilities of expansion which she submits to the Superior General. Together with her Council she proposes to the Superior General and her Council: Admission to the novitiate Admission to first profession Admission to perpetual profession Appointment of local Superior. She present the case where dismissal of a professed sister of temporary vows seems imperative. The Regional Superior

sections.title: Composition of Chapter
sections.text: The foundation of communities in a new country leads to the formation of Regions which are dependent on the Province that helped to form them, or on the Superior General and her Council if the Region is composed of religious from several Provinces. The Regional Superior is appointed by the Superior General with the consent of her Council after consultation with the sisters of the Region and the Provincial Superior, if the Region is dependent on a Province. The Regional Superior exercises authority delegated by the Superior General or by the Provincial Superior on whom she depends. The Regional Superior must be five years perpetually professed. Her term of office is three years, twice renewable. The Regional Superior, assisted by two Councilors, proposes to the Major Superior on whom she depends: Admissions to the postulancy, novitiate, first profession, perpetual profession Changes of assignment for the sisters Appointment of local Superiors. She visits the houses, authorizes expenses within the limits of her financial capacity, watches over the spiritual animation of the communities in the Region. When a Province has become too extensive, it may be divided into Regions in order to facilitate its government. The Provincial Superior retains authority over the whole Province. The Regional Assistants exercise the authority that is delegated to them by the Provincial Superior. The Local Superior

sections.title: Convocation of Chapter
sections.text: While the Sisters of St. Paul are members of the Congregation as a whole, they also belong to local communities which are for them the concrete expression of the vast fraternity of the Congregation. Each local community has a Superior through whom the community is drawn closely together in obedience. The local Superior possesses real authority though she may exercise it with simplicity. She receives the authority from God through the ministry of the Church upon her appointment by the Provincial Superior according to the Constitution. This authority is exercised in comformity with the commandment of the Lord as a service and it presupposes not only the participation of the sisters but also the decision of the Superior. The Local Superior must govern in accordance with the directives of the Church, the Book of Life, the Acts of the Chapters and the instructions of the Superior General and the Provincial Superior. When considering a choice of local Superiors, the Provincial Superiors will undertake a suitable consultation of the professed sisters of the Province (C 625) The Local Superior is appointed for three years by the Provincial Superior with the consent of her Council. She may be maintained in office for a second three-year term. The third term and, eventually, the forth, should be submitted to the Superior General and her Council after consultation (verbal for the third term and written for the fourth) with the sisters of the community concerned. The Local Superior must have two years of perpetual profession. Mission of the Local Superior

sections.title: Chapter Authority
sections.text: Because of the apostolic nature of the communities of the Sisters of St. Paul, the Superior has the basic responsibility to provide her community with the spiritual resources each sister needs for her apostolate; among these are the celebration of the Eucharist, community prayer and fraternal relationships. The apostolic spirit is fundamental to the unity of the community regardless of the mission of each member. Discretion, respect for persons and the desire for their spiritual good, characterize the trustful relations of the Superior with each of her sisters. She contributes to apostolic discernment, encourages initiative, and leaves each one her share of responsibility. The Superior is particularly solicitous for the sick or the aged sisters. She gives the younger sisters the support and formation they need. She encourages all the members of the community to continue their formation on both doctrinal and professional levels. The Superior is careful to foster in the community a great spirit of charity and union, and she has at heart the observance of the law of life of the Congregation. Each Superior may grant occasional dispensations to her sister in matters of everyday life. If these dispensations are of long duration or if their object is important, they shall be submitted to the Major Superior on whom the community depends. The Local Superior herself, or in cooperation with the local Bursar, watches over the administration of the temporal goods of the house. The Superior is a bond of unity among her own sisters and she also forms a bond with the other communities of the Province, by taking part in the meetings organized by the Provincial Superior, communicating information received and stimulating interest in everything that concerns the Congregation. When a young sister is on probation in a community, the Superior keeps up contact with the Directresses of Formation. Moreover, the Superiors facilitate contact between the sisters and their Major Superiors. The Superiors keep the chronicles updated in their houses. Attitude of the Local Superior

sections.title: Chapter Procedures
sections.text: The Superior prays for the courage to take such decisions as are necessary, and the daring to promote the service of God perseveringly on spite of contradiction. The Superior's own life is a witness in her community and this is vital and sometimes decisive for her sisters. Her love of the Congregation, assiduity in prayer, sacrifices accepted for the good of the community and the way she carries out her task, are an encouragement and an incentive. For a better apostolic service, the local Superior welcomes the suggestions of the sisters and she encourages them to cooperate actively with both clergy and laity. Local Council

sections.title: Provincial Chapter
sections.text: In small houses the local Council includes all the sisters. In the bigger houses, for better coordination, it is formed of those in charge of the different areas of activity. Appropriate organization should likewise enable all the sisters to participate in common reflective sharing, after which, the Superior makes the final decision. The local Council is appointed by the Provincial Superior after consultation with the sisters of the house.

sections.title: Provincial Chapter Composition
sections.text: The search for God's will has always animated the General Chapters which are landmarks in the history of the Congregation. Through its work and decisions, the General Chapter gives vital impetus to the whole body. The capitulars who represent all the sisters are attentive to the inspiration of the Spirit who raised up the Congregation and continues to sustain it. They form a fraternal assembly in Christ present among them through prayer, charity and the fidelity of all. Government in the Congregation is exercised in a continuous manner by the Superior General assisted by her Council whereas the General Chapter exercises supreme authority in the Institute for the duration of its legitimate session (C 631). The General Chapter has mission: to be vigilant in maintaining the charism and spirit of the Congregation, and to promote the renewals and adaptations necessary to live faithfully this spirit, to elect the Superior General and Assistants General, to evaluate the state of the Congregation on the spiritual, apostolic and financial levels, to determine the major orientations to be given for the common good. The ordinary General Chapter meets every six years or before this time if the office of Superior General is vacant. It may be convoked extraordinarily if the General Council and the Provincial Superiors judge it necessary. Should a major obstacle prevent the holding of the Chapter, the Superior General has recourse to the Holy See for the temporary prorogation of her powers and those of her Council. Convocation and Constitution of the General Chapter

sections.title: Provincial Chapter Authority
sections.text: At least six months in advance, the Superior General convokes the General Chapter, at the same time indicating the procedure for the election of the delegates. The members of the General Chapter are as follows: The Superior General and the Assistants General, the Secretary General and the Bursar General, the ex-Superiors General, the Provincial Superiors and the District Superiors, the delegates of Provinces, Districts and houses which depend on the General Council. The number of elected delegates will be at least equal to that of members by right. The General Chapter required the presence of two-thirds of the capitulars for the validity of its acts. The members of the General Chapter represent the entire Congregation. The capitulars, coming as they do from different provinces or countries and having varied competency, inform the Chapter; they do not specially represent the sisters who voted for them. The members of the Chapter retain complete freedom to express their viewpoints, each one speaking according to her conscience, without having to account for it later on. The Superior General announces by circular letter the approximate opening date of the General Chapter. Arrangements are made for a period of preparation before the convocation. The General Council prepares the subject for study and sends it throughout the Provinces and Districts. The Provincial Chapters are requested to present to the General Council the names of two or three persons who are qualified for general administration; however the Superior General has the right to consult the Provincial Superiors directly on the matter. Election of the Superior General

sections.title: Admission to Postulancy
sections.text: The capitulars, whose sole motive is the good of the Congregation, elect the person of their choice to direct the Institute. It is in prayer and reflection that they exercise this judgment, keenly aware of the responsibility that rests on them. The consultations require respect for persons and are incompatible with intrigue or pressure. The Superior General is elected for six years and may be re-elected for a second six-year term. She may be maintained in office for a third term of six years if she obtains two-thirds of the votes, with the possibility of three votings. The Superior General must have at least ten years of perpetual profession and be at least forty years of age. To be elected, the Superior General must obtain the absolute majority of votes. If after the first ballot no one obtains an absolute majority, a second shall be held or even a third if necessary. After the third ballot in which no one obtained an absolute majority, a fourth ballot shall follow where only the two sisters who obtained the highest number of votes in the third ballot or if they are more than two, the two senior by age are eligible (C 119). These two sisters have no right to vote at the fourth ballot. If the two sisters obtain the same number of votes at this fourth ballot, the senior according to first profession is elected; if they made profession the same day, the senior according to age is elected. If the Superior General elect is absent, she is summoned. The Chapter sessions are suspended until her arrival. Election of the Assistants

sections.title: Admission to Novitiate
sections.text: The newly elected Superior General presides over the election of the four Assistants. The first Assistants elected will replace the Superior General when the latter is absent or impeded. The Superior General and the Assistants General remain in office until the next General Chapter, except in the case of a major impediment. The election of the Assistants General is carried out in separate balloting by absolute majority; however, if no sister obtains this majority in the first two ballots, a third will be taken where the sister who obtains a relative majority will be elected. In case of a tie in this third ballot, the senior according to profession will be elected, but in case of equality of profession, the senior according to age will be elected. Acts, Decisions and Limitations of the General Chapter

sections.title: Admission to Vows
sections.text: On opening the General Chapter, the Superior General presents a report on the apostolic and religious state of the Congregation. The Assistants General and the Provincial Superiors for their respective Province may be invited to present various reports. Examination of Bursar General's books of account is confided to a commission elected by the Chapter. Then, the capitulars are given the study material together with the relevant documents. They eventually revise the Statutes or the Capitular Acts elaborated by previous Chapters. The capitulars work in an atmosphere of intensive prayer. In fidelity to the charism of the origins and to the Book of Life, they are careful to follow the Church in all things. Because the General Chapter has responsibility to promote the greater good of the Congregation, the acts of the Chapter are directed to spiritual, community and apostolic progress. One in mind and heart, the capitulars pursue their work, striving to achieve unanimity - sign of the presence of the Holy Spirit. The resolutions of the General Chapter remain in force until the following Chapter. A modification of the Constitutions will require a two- thirds vote of the capitulars before it is submitted to Holy See. The mode of adopting decisions (absolute majority parity of suffrage) specified by a procedure which is subject to revision at the close of the Chapter in anticipation of the next Chapter. The mission and powers of the General Chapter cease the moment the Superior General, with the consent of the absolute majority of the capitulars, pronounces it closed. Council of Congregation

sections.title: Voluntary Departure
sections.text: The Superior General convenes the Council of Congregation once between two General Chapters and whenever she considers it useful. The Council of Congregation, presided over by the Superior General, is composed of the Assistants General and the Provincial and District Superiors. This Council was organized for the purpose of consultation, participation and the sharing of information. Research and realizations are put in common in view of the general good and greater unity within the Congregation. Adaptation to the needs of the times is enhanced through fraternal reflection and sharing for better service of the Gospel in the world.

sections.title: Dismissal
sections.text: The Provincial Superior, after consultation which her Council and in agreement with the Superior General, convokes the Provincial Chapter which must meet before the General Chapter. The preparation and organization of the Provincial Chapter are undertaken by the Provincial Superior and her Council. This fraternal assembly, representing a Province, is presided over by the Provincial Superior and is composed of the Provincial Council members, the Directress of the Novitiate and of the Juniorate as well as the delegated elected by the sisters. The Provincial Chapter, while studying the questions that directly concern it, never forgets that it belongs to the universal body of the Congregation. The presence of the Superior General or of an Assistant General tends to encourage communication between the Provincial and the general levels. Election of Delegated to the Provincial Chapter

sections.title: Departure Procedures
sections.text: The election of the delegates to the Provincial Chapter is made from a single list of the perpetually professed sisters (Superiors and sisters), who are not members by right. The delegated to the Provincial Chapter are chosen without distinction from among the sisters or Superiors. The proportion is one delegate to twelve sisters of perpetual profession, or fraction of twelve greater than six. The elections consist of two ballots. The sisters who obtain the absolute majority of votes in the first ballot are elected. The list of all the sisters who obtained votes will be published. But in order to have a certain concentration of votes for the second ballot, the Provincial Council will draw up the list of sisters eligible for the second ballot. This is determined by the percentage of votes obtained in the first ballot in proportion to the remaining number of delegated to be elected. On the second ballot, the sisters are elected by a relative majority of votes. When a Province is divided into Regions, the Provincial Superior, assisted by her Council divides the number of delegates to be elected, proportionally to the size of the Regions. She draws up a list for each Region. The election of the delegated to the Provincial Chapter will be held at least six months before the General Chapter in order to give time for the election of delegates to the General Chapter. In case of death or major impediment of any delegate to the Provincial Chapter, the Provincial Council will see to her replacement. When the Provincial Council is changed, a partial election shall be held to complete the number of delegates. Mission of the Provincial Chapter

sections.title: Administration of Goods
sections.text: The Provincial Chapter has the mission to prepare for the forthcoming General Chapter and to elect delegates to it. The Provincial Chapter studies the implementation of the directives of the General Chapter and submits its resolutions to the Superior General and her Council. The Provincial Chapter has no legislative power. In the same spirit as the General Chapter, the members of the Provincial Chapter implore the help of the Holy Spirit so as to seek the will of God before all else. The Provincial capitulars are faithful to the directives of the Church, the spirit of the Congregation, the Book of Life and the decisions of the General Chapter. In close union with God, the strive to be one in spirit, sign of their charity and upright intention. Election of Delegated to the General Chapter

sections.title: Temporal Administrators
sections.text: All the Provinces send to the General Chapter, besides the Provincial Superior, two delegates elected by the Provincial Chapter. If there are more than two hundred and fifty sisters of perpetual vows, an additional delegate is elected for every group of one hundred and fifty sisters (or a number less than one hundred and fifty but more than fifty). The Districts send besides the District Superior, one elected delegate. The elections of the delegates to the General Chapter are carried out in separate ballots. The delegates may be chosen from among all the sisters of perpetual profession of the Province. The absolute majority of votes is required for the election of the delegates in the first and second ballot. If the absolute majority is not obtained in the second ballot, a third ballot is taken. The sister who obtains the greatest number of votes is elected. Council of Province

sections.title: Financial Accountability
sections.text: The Council of Province, which the Provincial Superior convokes every year, brings together the Provincial Assistants, the Secretary, the Bursar and the local Superiors. This Council brings up for discussion matters treating of consecrated life, apostolate, formation and administration. It ensures greater unity of action. From time to time, the Superior General or an Assistant General, if available, takes part in the Council of Province. An Inter-Provincial Council is not part of the government structures of the Congregation but it may play a role in the unity of life between Provinces of the same country. The functioning of this Council may vary according to the countries.

sections.title: Revision of Constitutions
sections.text: On the local level, the Superior encourages fraternal sharing. The community meetings give the sisters an opportunity to inform one another and to discuss matters of a practical order. Examination of their community life-style, reflection on apostolic activities and spiritual sharing will be fruitful if they lead to a permanent conversion of mind. The members of the community learn to respect and love one another, in spite of their diversity, source of mutual enrichment. Although moments of tension or trial sometimes constitute a threat to fraternal unity, they can become an occasion of grace strengthening in each one the gift of self made to Christ Jesus.

sections.title: Amendments
sections.text: The book of life and Statutes is the rule of life of the Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres. The Book of life which the Holy See has approved cannot be modified without its authorization. The Statutes may be revised by the General Chapters. The authentic interpretation of the Constitutions is reserved to the Holy See. The sisters, by their profession in the Congregation, promise to put into practice the Book of Life and Statutes. This book concerns their whole life and mission in the Community, in the Church and in the world. God pursues his plan for the Congregation and for each member in spite of the obscurity of our earthly condition. Faithful to her rule of life, and with her eyes fixed on Christ Jesus her Model, the Sister of St. Paul strains ahead to the finish, while her whole life proclaims to others the coming of the Kingdom.
